projects.title: Guardian (Calhacks 12.0 Winner)
projects.description: Guardian helps users stay financially secure with instant alerts, simple explanations, and peace of mind in under a second. As sole frontend engineer, I designed and developed a sleek React + Figma interface integrating five AI systems (Anthropic, Bright Data, OpenAI, Fetch, FishAudio) into one seamless experience with a voice-first experience/emphasis for elderly users' ease (easier to digest content and info).How It Works:Guardian’s modular system combines AI-powered anomaly detection with natural-language and voice technology to identify and explain risky transactions in seconds:A Python Flask backend runs an unsupervised anomaly-detection model (SHAP-based) that flags abnormal purchases based on features like spending pattern, frequency, and location.Bright Data’s web-scraping API enriches the model with live merchant-reputation signals and consumer complaint trends. When risk is detected, Anthropic’s Claude generates a simple, empathetic explanation tailored for seniors, and Fish Audio converts it into a calm, humanlike voice alert.Fetch.ai agents automate next steps like dispute preparation or double-charge checks.The React + Figma interface presents everything visually: a readable transcript, risk level, and two large action buttons, “Mark Safe” or “Block”, keeping users in control.Relevance/Impact:Guardian addresses a growing crisis of financial fraud, affecting over 75% of Americans. By merging machine learning with accessible design, it empowers vulnerable populations, especially seniors, to protect their money independently. The platform not only prevents fraud but also restores confidence in digital finance through instant transparency and emotional reassurance.APIs/Platforms/Tools:React, Python Flask, Bright Data, Claude (Anthropic), Fish Audio, Fetch.ai, Django, SQL, Render, Figma, CSS3, JavaScript, WhiteNoise, Cursor.Recognition:1st Place Winner, Bright Data API Track at CalHacks 12.0 (3000+ participants, 700+ projects, $2000 prize).

projects.title: Orca (Weavehacks)
projects.description: Four worker LLMs play an abstract Minecraft-lite tech-tree game (wood → stone → iron →... → portal → dragon). A fifth model — Orca, the manager — never touches the controls. Between episodes it reads the team's trace, decides who should do what, coaches each worker in plain language, and keeps an edit only if it measurably helps. Orca's delegation policy is a bandit; the workers improve verbally (they rewrite their own how-to memory). Our model of two learners and two timescales is exactly what kills the instability that sinks naive multi-agent RL.The headline: train Orca on seeds {A, T2, T3}, freeze it, then test on never-seen seeds {B, C}. The full system roughly triples both baselines on the held-out seeds — and shows no gap between training and held-out performance. It generalized and it didn't just use "brute force" to memorize the map.my role:RL env and Reward Systems Engineer: Owned the full environment/reward layer in a simulated Minecraft-style DAG world; drove team invalid-action rate from 0.3 to 0.06 Engineered a 35-region multi-layer world graph with bearing-only perception and a coordinate-leak invariant, a full crafting tech tree, superadditive cooperative combat (solo ~20% vs. coordinated ~85% success) to incentivize delegation, and survival mechanics (hunger, death/respawn, day/night)Implemented a seeded world generator and a full-DAG scripted oracle that reaches end-state on all 5 seeds, and a winnability validator and greedy baseline establishing the ground-truth benchmark the learned manager is measured against; delivered 320+ passing tests across env/reward suite with zero regressions thru a green-main integration gate, proving manager learns coordination, not memorizing maps (.87 mean frontier vs .31 baselines)

projects.title: TETHER (SBHacks, TwelveLabs Showcase Invitational)
projects.description: Built “T-ETHER,” a video learning tool featuring semantic indexing and key-moment discovery. Served as lead frontend engineer (and supporting full-stack), designing and implementing core UI and UX in Figma/React for quick navigation, interactive exploration, and structured takeaways. Integrated TwelveLabs’ APIs: Marengo for multimodal searches to locate key moments, Pegasus for instant higher-level generative summary and comprehension. Invited afterwards (out of 39 other projects) to present at TwelveLabs’ developer webinar showcase series.
